# 04 — Configuration Files

All configuration lives in `config/`. Files with year suffixes (`-2022`, `-2023`, `-2024v2`,
`-2025v2`, …) are archived past-season configurations kept as examples; only the un-suffixed
files are loaded. `*.template.json` files are documentation templates. `stuff.json` is empty.

## `config.json` (server, generated by the setup wizard, git-ignored)

```jsonc
{
  "secrets": {
    "ACCESS_CODE": "string",        // admin/setup/edit/schedule password (may be absent → no auth)
    "DATABASE_URL": "mongodb://...", // required
    "TBA_API_KEY": "string",        // required for schedules/teams/OPR; warned if missing
    "FMS_API_USERNAME": "string",   // optional; FRC Events API basic-auth
    "FMS_API_KEY": "string",        // optional
    "GOOGLE_AUTH": { "CLIENT_ID": "", "CLIENT_SECRET": "" }, // template only; Google sign-in non-functional
    "GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID": "", "GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET": ""      // setup form fields (disabled inputs)
  },
  "VERSION": "1.0",                 // client data version stamped on TMPs (hidden form field)
  "TBA_EVENT_KEY": "2026mnwi",      // active TBA event key
  "EVENT_NUMBER": "69a5ac…",        // ObjectId hex of the active events document
  "DEMO": false,                    // demo mode
  "SWAP_ZONE_BUTTON_LOCATIONS": false, // swap AZone/OAZone grid positions and rotate field map
  "TBA_OPR_STRINGS": { "string_1": "Hub Total Fuel Count", "string_2": "minorFoulCount", ... }
}
```

- **CF-1** `secrets` is stripped when served to clients at `/config/config.json`.
- **CF-2** Boolean fields may arrive as `true`/`"true"`/`"on"`; clients parse all three.
- **CF-3a** **[A-14]** The Filter Teams rating bands and OPR ranges (document 08, AN-19)
  must become configuration rather than constants.
- **CF-3** `TBA_OPR_STRINGS` values must exactly match TBA COPR key names; keys are
  `string_N` in order. The setup page defaults to six 2026 keys: `Hub Total Fuel Count`,
  `minorFoulCount`, `majorFoulCount`, `Hub Auto Fuel Count`, `Hub Teleop Fuel Count`,
  `Hub Uncounted`.
- **CF-4** `EVENT_NUMBER` is presented in the setup UI as the event **code** string and converted
  to/from ObjectId by the setup API.

## `match-scouting.json` (scouting UI)

```jsonc
{
  "timing": {
    "totalTime": 160000,                       // milliseconds (older configs used seconds in the template; runtime treats as ms)
    "timeTransitions": {
      "<msRemaining>": {
        "layer": 1,                            // layer index to show when time <= key
        "displayText": "Auto",                 // phase label; also the action-id prefix source
        "variables": { "name": "value" },      // optional: variable values set at this transition
        "conditional": { "<var>": { "<value>": ["buttonId", ...] } }, // optional conditional rendering
        "always": ["buttonId", ...]            // optional: buttons always rendered in that layer
      }
    }
  },
  "variables": { "minOfQueueLength": 2, "<anyName>": "<initialValue>" },
  "layout": {
    "gridRows": 6,
    "gridColumns": 11,
    "layers": [ [ Button, ... ], [ Button, ... ], ... ]
  }
}
```

Button object:

```jsonc
{
  "id": "StartShooting",                  // action id (may repeat across layers; same id behaves identically)
  "displayText": "Start Scoring",          // button label (defaults to id); "\n" allowed
  "gridArea": ["4", "2", "5", "6"],        // CSS grid-area parts: row-start / col-start / row-end / col-end
  "class": "fuel2026",                     // space-separated CSS classes
  "type": "action" | "undo" | "none" | "match-control" | "label",
  "executables": [ { "type": "layer", "args": [7, 10] }, ... ]
}
```

- **CF-5** `timeTransitions` keys are numeric strings compared against remaining time; they
  fire in descending order once `time <= key`. The first transition (largest key) supplies
  the initial `displayText` when the match starts. **[A-40]** `totalTime` and keys are
  **milliseconds only**; the Configuration Guide's "seconds" is wrong and the rewrite must not
  accept both. **BL-298** A transition should also be able to declare a timer hold
  (`pauseMs`) for the field-timer pause between auto and teleop.
- **CF-6** `variables.minOfQueueLength` is **required** by the undo guard (undo only when
  `actionQueue.length > minOfQueueLength`; with the temp `startGame` entry this means at least
  one real action must exist). `variables` must exist (the client iterates its keys).
- **CF-7** Every button MUST have `class` (string), `gridArea` (array), `executables`
  (array, may be empty), and `type`. `displayText` optional.
- **CF-8** Special ids recognized by the client: `AZone` and `OAZone` (alliance zone
  swapping), `teleopActive` and `teleopInactive` (shift toggles, must be `type: "none"`),
  any button whose id/label normalizes to contain `astop` (A-Stop lock). Layer lookups use
  `teleopActive`'s `layer` executable target to find the "teleop layer".
- **CF-9** A layer that is never navigated to may be used as an **id catalog** so that
  composite ids (`activeShift1StopShooting`, …) are known to `countActions` (`all: true`)
  and to the QR id enumeration. The 2026 config uses layer index 12 for this (195 buttons).
  **[A-23]** This was a hack; the rewrite MUST replace it with an explicit `knownActionIds`
  list (or derive the set from phase prefixes × button ids) in configuration.
  **Done in schema v2** (document 20, CS-5): ids are derived from prefixes × action buttons
  plus `extraActionIds`; the converter removes the catalog layer.
- **CF-9a** **[A-22]** The composite-id scheme (phase prefix + button id) was new in 2026 and
  configs depend on it; the rewrite should keep the recorded ids compatible while looking for
  a generic way to express phases/shifts in config (see document 05, SC-22/23).
- **CF-9b** **[A-51]** Button `class` names may be replaced by explicit colors in the schema;
  a converter for old configs is optional. **Done in schema v2** (CS-8; converter exists).
- **CF-9c** **BL-60** The position-lock delay must be configurable. **Done in schema v2**
  (`rules.positionLockMs`, CS-9).

> **Schema v2.** This document describes the v1 (legacy) files, which are kept in `config/v1/`.
> The v6 application reads the v2 files in `config/` described in document 20; the semantics
> below still apply unless document 20 says otherwise.

Executable catalog (`type` → `args`), see document 05 for behavior:

| type                     | args                                              | Purpose                                                                                  |
| ------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `layer`                  | `[fromLayer, toLayer]`                            | Show `toLayer`; undo returns to previous rendered set                                    |
| `conditionalLayer`       | `[from, to, alwaysRender[], conditionalRender{}]` | Show `to` filtering buttons by variables                                                 |
| `conditionalLayerUndo`   | same                                              | Identical implementation (misnamed duplicate)                                            |
| `setVariable`            | `[name, value]`                                   | Set a variable (undo restores previous)                                                  |
| `position`               | `[]`                                              | Capture field position into `other.pos` with 1 s position lock                           |
| `constantPosition`       | `[{x,y}]`                                         | Attach a fixed `other.pos`                                                               |
| `climbHighlight`         | `[...ids]` (args unused)                          | Highlight this button, un-highlight other climbHighlight buttons; undo restores previous |
| `clearHighlight`         | `[]`                                              | Remove highlight from this button; undo restores                                         |
| `hide`                   | `[]`                                              | Hide the button; undo shows it                                                           |
| `multiplier`             | `[n]`                                             | Push `n-1` extra copies of the action (action buttons only)                              |
| `flashBorder`, `example` | —                                                 | No-ops (templates)                                                                       |

## `qr.json`

```jsonc
{
  "ACTION_SCHEMA": [
    { "key": "id", "bits": 8 },
    { "key": "ts", "bits": 32 },
  ],
}
```

- **CF-10** Defines the per-action bit layout for QR encoding/decoding. `id` must be first and
  is encoded as an enumeration index (max `2^bits - 2`); other keys are parsed as integers
  (max `2^bits - 1`). The decoder reads `key` values by `getVal(action, key)` so nested keys
  are technically allowed by the encoder but the decoder only assigns top-level keys.

## `analysis-pipeline.json`

An ordered array of transformer instances:

```jsonc
[
  { "type": "tmp" | "team", "name": "countActions", "outputPath": "counts", "options": { ... } },
  ...
]
```

- **CF-11** Executed strictly in order on the client (analysis page) and on the server (CSV
  export). `tmp` transformers should precede `team` transformers that depend on them.
- **CF-12** `name` must match a transformer file name in `src/analysis/transformers/`;
  `type` must match a `__TMP__`/`__TEAM__` block in that file.
- **CF-12a** **[A-41]** The `cycle` transformer's option names are `startAction`/`endAction`/
  `misses`; the guide's `pickups`/`scores` are out of date and need not be supported.
  **[A-3]** Archived year configs are not required fixtures, but the documented structure and
  best practices of `analysis-pipeline.json` should be preserved.
- **CF-13** The Configuration Guide marks as **required** for full feature coverage:
  `tmp/countActions(all)` → `counts`, per-phase `scores.*` weighted sums and `scores.total`,
  `team/countActions(all)` → `counts`, `team/standardDeviation(scores.total)` →
  `standardDeviation`, `team/average(counts)` → `averages`, `team/average(scores)` →
  `averageScores`. The CSV export requires `averages`, `averageScores`, and `cycles` on every
  team with data; the bubble graph defaults to the first three keys of `averageScores`;
  match prediction uses `averageScores.total` and `standardDeviation`. The shipped 2026
  pipeline omits `standardDeviation` and `scores.total` because Simulate Match is disabled.

## `analysis-modules.json`

An array of module instances:

```jsonc
{
  "view": "team" | "match",
  "module": "Stats" | "Bar" | "Pie" | "HeatmapScatterPlot" | "RadarChart" | "PerformanceTimePlot" | "SingleDisplay" | "ColumnDisplay" | "Grid" | "Divider",
  "position": "main" | "side",        // team view column (match view ignores)
  "name": "Team Stats",               // title
  "separate": false,                  // optional: show module even for teams with no data
  "wholeMatch": false,                // optional (match view): receive both alliances joined by "|"
  "options": { ... }                  // module-specific (document 09)
}
```

- **CF-14** Team-view modules are instantiated once each; match-view modules are instantiated
  twice (left/right alliance). The `side` column is enabled only if any module has
  `position: "side"`.

## `analysis-transformers.json`

Describes how the transformer bundle is compiled:

```jsonc
{
  "template": { "file": "_template.template.js", "placeholder": "__TRANSFORMERS__" },
  "template2": { "file": "_template2.template.js", "placeholder": "__TRANSFORMERS__" },
  "types": [
    { "name": "tmp", "identifier": "TMP", "data": "" },
    { "name": "team", "identifier": "TEAM", "data": "" },
  ],
  "ignore": ["_template2.template.js", "transformers.md"],
}
```

- **NOTE** The file defines `types` and `ignore` twice (JSON duplicate keys; last wins), so
  `_template.template.js` is not in the effective ignore list. It still works because that
  file contains no `__TMP__` markers.

## `src/analysis/manual/teams.json`, `tmps.json`

Hooks for hand-entered data merged into the dataset (`manual.*` paths, `manual: true` TMPs).
Both ship empty (`{}` and `[]`). Team modules treat a team whose only key is `manual` as
"no data" (module hidden unless `separate: true`).

## `config/configInfo.md`

Legacy description of a `client.json` (pre-split of `config.json`/`match-scouting.json`).
Retained as documentation of the button schema only.
